title: Session Reroute, Predictive Prefetch & Telemetry Playbook (PRD Draft)
content:
Context:
This doc captures a pragmatic PRD-level proposal and a playbook for (1) session reroute semantics when requests must failover across model variants/regions/capacity tiers, (2) predictive prefetch strategies to hide cold-model latency for common tool-call patterns, and (3) a minimal telemetry schema and SDK ergonomics required to make both observable and safe for integrations.

Why now?
- Customers building multi-step agent flows and tool-choreography see tail latency spikes when primary replicas are saturated or when downgrading to quantized/fast models.
- Existing hosted streaming surface covers partial-response ergonomics but lacks a first-class pattern for transparent reroutes with deterministic client-side resume.
- We can significantly reduce perceived latency with light predictive prefetch for tool invocation (e.g., knowledge-base fetch, web-search) without bloating cost if paired with telemetry-informed heuristics.

Objectives (success criteria):
- Provide a deterministic, resumable session reroute protocol for streaming responses such that developer-visible divergence is minimized and recovery is transparent to end users (SLO: 95% of rerouted sessions do not require app-level reconciliation).
- Reduce median observed time-to-first-tool-result in mixed workloads by 20–40% for customers with frequent tool calls.
- Produce a compact telemetry schema (<= 10 required fields) enabling routing decisions and capacity signals without leaking PII.
- SDK ergonomics: add minimal surface area changes so client upgrades are low friction and offline emulation is possible.

Non-goals:
- Full automatic semantic reconciliation of partially-applied tool effects (out of scope; apps must handle idempotency).
- Building a generic prefetch for arbitrary long-running tools (we scope to network-bound tool calls <10s).

Key concepts and terminology:
- session-id: stable identifier for an application-level conversation.
- checkpoint: small snapshot token returned periodically to clients during streaming that can be used to resume on reroute.
- reroute: server-initiated or client-requested migration of a session to a compatible target (model variant/region/tier).
- predictive-prefetch: speculative invocation of a tool based on the model's intent signal before an explicit toolcall finalization.

Proposed protocol (high level):
1) Streaming with check-pointed frames: server emits compact checkpoint frames every N tokens (configurable, default ~128 tokens) containing: session-id, checkpoint-id, last-ack-offset, model-variant, compact safety hash.
2) Client-side ACK and hedging window: SDK periodically acknowledges checkpoint-id; the server records last-acked checkpoint. If the server detects capacity issues, it may signal a reroute with a reroute-frame and a target capability set (e.g., {model: fast-quant, region: eu-west-1, supports-tools: true}).
3) Reroute sequence: the client SDK automatically attempts reconnect to the target endpoint with the last-acked checkpoint, requests any missing prefix tokens or a compact resynthesis plan from server side. The server may accept compact resume or reject (server returns resume_reject with a recommended fallback sequence).
4) Deterministic resume: to avoid semantic divergence, resume is limited to a set of compatible transitions (exact same tokenizer and deterministic seeds). Where lossiness is expected (quantized model variants), the server marks resume as lossy and includes a confidence delta metric to the client.

Predictive prefetch design:
- Model signal: the runtime tags intermediate tokens with an intent_score and tentative-tool-spec when the model strongly indicates a tool will be called (thresholded).
- Prefetch policy: SDK (opt-in per-route) will speculatively fire the tool if intent_score > X and either: client allows speculative-prefetch=true OR the route has prefetch-credits. Prefetch results are cached with short TTL (default 30s) and attached when the final tool call is confirmed.
- Cost control: prefetches are billed as "prefetch units" and charged lower (or free under credits) for first N prefetches/user per minute — policy configurable by customer tier.

SDK ergonomics (recommended minimal surface):
- sessionResume(token: string): exposed to developers for manual control but SDK auto-resumes by default.
- onCheckpoint(callback): give developers visibility into checkpoint frames for custom telemetry or persistence.
- enablePredictivePrefetch(boolean | policy): opt-in flag with defaults off; policy can specify TTL, max speculative-per-minute.
- prefetchEvent hooks: events for prefetchStarted, prefetchCompleted, prefetchCancelled.
- resumeMetadata in streaming event: exposes resume_is_lossy, confidence_delta, target_variant.

Telemetry schema (required fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- session_id
- checkpoint_id
- event_type (checkpoint|reroute|prefetch_started|prefetch_result|resume_result)
- model_variant
- region
- latency_ms (for the event or tool call)
- prefetch_cost_units (optional numeric string)
- resume_is_lossy (true|false)
- correlation_id (for cross-service tracing)
Notes: keep sizes small, prefer hashed identifiers, no raw prompt text in required telemetry fields.

Fallback and safety considerations:
- If resume is rejected or marked lossy above a threshold, SDK surfaces a clear developer callback with the raw recommended recovery steps (e.g., request full re-run, escalate to manual merge).
- Prefetch data must be treated as ephemeral: expiration TTL and strict sandboxing; tools must support a way to indicate preliminary semantics so callers don't commit prefetch results until confirmation.
- Privacy: prefetch only allowed for tools annotated as "non-sensitive" by the customer (administrative control).

Operationalizing and rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA):
MVP (8 weeks):
- Implement checkpoint frames in streaming runtime + simple reroute frame.
- SDK: auto-resume using last-acked checkpoint, onCheckpoint hook.
- Telemetry: ingest basic events into observability pipeline.
- Prefetch: server-side intent-score emit only, no automatic prefetch.

Beta (12 weeks):
- Add predictive prefetch opt-in in SDK and server-side prefetch orchestration.
- Billing prototype for prefetch units (internal charge).
- Add resume_is_lossy flag and confidence_delta telemetry.

GA (additional 8–12 weeks):
- Fine-grained customer policies (per-route prefetch budgets, tiered pricing).
- Admin UI and console signals for prefetch hotspots and reroute incidents.

Metrics to track:
- reroute_rate (per 1k sessions) and reroute_success_rate (percent auto-resumed without app intervention).
- median_time_to_tool_result with and without prefetch enabled.
- prefetch_hit_rate (speculative prefetch used vs wasted).
- average extra cost per 1k prefetch units.
- developer adoption: % of SDK-enabled routes enabling predictive prefetch.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Checkpoint frequency: trade latency vs state size. Default 128 tokens is a starting point but needs real workload profiling.
- Prefetch billing semantics: should prefetch be a first-class cheap unit or consumed from regular tool budgets?
- Resume semantics across quantization types: how tolerant are typical apps to small divergence? We should run focused experiments.
- Security: need a per-customer allowlist for tools eligible for speculative prefetch (corporate security policies).

Implementation notes / engineering tasks (draft):
- runtime: add checkpoint frame emission, reroute control frame hooks, compact resume API (IDP).
- routing: extend policy engine to include reroute reasons (capacity|latency|failover) and target capability sets.
- sdk: add resume flow, hooks, and opt-in prefetch API. Ensure offline emulation mode for devs.
- observability: implement telemetry schema and retention rules; add dashboard tiles for reroute incidents and prefetch economics.

Doc/comms:
- Internal runbook (SRE) for reroute incidents and how to triage.
- Customer-facing docs: opt-in guide for predictive prefetch, best practices for idempotent tool calls.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Engineering spike: quantize resume experiments on toy models (2 weeks) — Diego + SRE.
- SDK prototype: implement onCheckpoint & auto-resume (4 weeks) — DExp (Ava lead).
- Telemetry pipeline: add event types and sampling rules (3 weeks) — Observability.
- Product review: gather 3 enterprise customers for privacy/prefetch policy feedback (PM outreach).

Appendix: sample streaming event (pseudo)
- checkpoint frame: {"event_type":"checkpoint","session_id":"s_123","checkpoint_id":"c_42","model_variant":"rwd-large-v1","offset":1024} (note: IDs will be hashed)
- reroute frame: {"event_type":"reroute","from_variant":"rwd-large-v1","to_variant":"rwd-fast-quant-v1","last_acked_checkpoint":"c_42","reason":"capacity","resume_expected":true}

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and conservative — we aim to avoid surprising application-level semantics while materially improving perceived latency for tool-first flows. Feedback requested on policy defaults (checkpoint cadence, prefetch TTL) and billing model for speculative work.
